text.p: Australia took six wickets in one session to dismiss West Indies for 304 and secure a first innings lead of 27 runs in the second test on Sunday.
Fast bowlers Glenn McGrath and Jason Gillespie and wrist spinner Shane Warne each took two wickets as the tourists added 75 runs during the afternoon session.
The two sides took an early tea break at the Sydney Cricket Ground after Warne wrapped up the West Indies innings by dismissing fast bowler Ian Bishop for 48.
It was Bishop's highest score in test cricket and featured six fours during an entertaining 95-minute stay at the crease.
Bishop was eventually caught by Australia opener Matthew Elliott at deep mid-wicket as he attempted to bring up his half-century with another boundary.
McGrath triggered the collapse by removing left-hander Jimmy Adams for 30 and wicketkeeper Courtney Browne for a duck in the fourth over after lunch with the total on 229.
Warne struck 14 runs later to dismiss Shivnarine Chanderpaul, who scored 48 in a stylish innings before chipping an attempted drive straight back to the bowler.
West Indies added a meagre 67 runs during the morning session against an accurate and unyielding Australian bowling attack for the loss of number four Carl Hooper for 27.
The tourists, who lost the first test in Brisbane by 123 runs, made slow progress throughout the day.
Hooper perfectly illustrated their difficulties, staying locked on his overnight score of 27 for 34 balls before being trapped leg before wicket by Warne without playing a shot with the total on 166.
McGrath finished with figures of four for 82 while Warne took three for 65.
Gillespie claimed his first wicket in test cricket when he bowled Curtly Ambrose for nine, a feat he repeated shortly after to dismiss Kenneth Benjamin.
